childcareContrast.note: the childcare indicator equals 0 for a measured 0.5% share of the sample (childcareContrast.indicatorZeroShare), so its coefficient is a near-degenerate contrast and its sign must not be read as an access effect; the group is attributed here

clusteredStandardErrors.estimator: statsmodels OLS cov_type='cluster' (cluster-robust CRVE), groups=project_name, statsmodels' default finite-cluster corrections; coefficients identical to the HC1 fit, only the covariance differs
clusteredStandardErrors.why: transactions inside one project share one location and project-level unobservables, so HC1's independence assumption is the wrong uncertainty model here; the HC1-vs-clustered comparison (indicatorCoefficients .clusterVsHC1SeRatio) is the measured demonstration of how much it understates

controls: area_sqft (square feet of strata area, continuous)
freehold indicator (1 when the tenure string is exactly 'Freehold')
long-lease indicator (1 when the parsed lease duration is at least 100 years; covers the 999-year and similar long-lease strings)

lease commencement year ((year-1900)/100, continuous; defined for parsed leasehold rows and set to 0 for freehold rows — the freehold indicator separates the groups, so this coefficient is identified from leasehold variation)
floor-band fixed effects (17 levels observed in the sample; baseline '01 to 05'; '-' is the unreported-band level, kept as its own level and never read as a storey number)
property-subtype fixed effects (3 levels: Apartment, Condominium, Executive Condominium; baseline 'Condominium')
transaction-type fixed effects (Resale/New Sale/Sub Sale; baseline 'Resale')
transaction-year fixed effects (baseline '2021'; absorb nominal price drift and inflation)
planning-area fixed effects (41 levels observed in the sample; baseline 'BUKIT TIMAH')
estimator.functionalForm: log-linear; coefficients are log points, and pctEffectExpMinus1 = 100*(exp(beta)-1) is the approximate percentage difference the log point implies
estimator.indicators: each access indicator enters as dist <= 1000 m in the shipped snapshot feature; ALL five indicators are fitted jointly in ONE specification (no selection, no stepwise search)
estimator.internalScaling: area_sqft/100 and (lease commencement year-1900)/100 for numerical stability; the indicators and dummies are unscaled, and the control coefficients below are back-transformed to natural units
estimator.name: OLS (statsmodels OLS, HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance, use_t=False)
notControlled: project identity (no project fixed effects — see projectEffects)
project completion year (the shipped year_completed column is null for all but a measured handful of condo rows; see sample.yearCompletedNullRows)
in-house facility presence (the subject of the legacy study; the layer is absent from this checkout)
unit condition, renovation, view and orientation
floor level WITHIN a floor band (bands are controlled, not storeys)
tenure gradations beyond the freehold and long-lease flags (9999/999999 lease-duration codes are not separated)
new-sale incentive structures and buyer financing
walking-path distance to the access features; access quality
planning-area x year shocks (the access indicators correlate with neighbourhood change inside a planning area)
the access snapshot's own vintage (one undated snapshot per layer; see RS04's amenity-impact audit for the vintage semantics)
estimator.projectEffects: NOT conditioned on: the specification carries no project fixed effects, so every coefficient here is a BETWEEN-PROJECT association — it compares transactions of projects that differ in the indicator with transactions of projects that do not, and cannot separate an access attribute from the project-level characteristics (location quality within the planning area, age, tenure mix, build quality, branding) that move with it. projectStructure quantifies this on the same sample. A project-fixed-effects specification is recorded as notFitted, not run
estimator.response: log(price per square foot); price in nominal Singapore dollars per square foot of strata area (shipped psf column; its identity with price/area_sqft is measured in responseLineage)
estimator.standardErrors: two batteries reported for every coefficient: (1) HC1 robust (unclustered — treats transactions as independent) and (2) project-clustered CRVE (see clusteredStandardErrors). The clustered battery is the published uncertainty; the HC1 battery is retained only to show the scale of the clustering understatement

definition: A measured source audit and one descriptive conditional-association model. The in-house facility layer the legacy study analysed (project facilities such as pools, gyms, tennis courts, sky gardens) is ABSENT from this checkout: the four legacy-named sources do not exist here, and the shipped dataset's only facility-like columns are external SportSG public-facility distances, a different subject. No facility premium is fitted, re-measured or claimed. What is measured: the recovered join key (project_name) and its coverage; per-facility no-record status (no-record is not absent and not zero); a between/within-project decomposition of log price-psf variance; and one recorded OLS of log condo price-psf on five jointly-fitted external-access indicators (shipped distance <= 1000 m) with stated controls and HC1 and project-clustered standard errors (cluster = project_name; the clustered battery is the published uncertainty and the HC1 battery is retained only to show the scale of the clustering understatement). That model does not condition on project identity: it is a BETWEEN-PROJECT comparison, and the measured variance decomposition is the quantification of what that means. Coefficients are conditional associations, not premiums and not causal effects; the access features come from one undated snapshot per layer joined to transactions from 2021-01 onward (see RS04's snapshot-join audit for the vintage semantics), so no coefficient compares amenity states at two dates. This ledger records one specification and only that one was fitted, and all its coefficients are reported; there is no dated prior protocol, so specification search cannot be ruled out — the single-specification discipline is a disclosed limitation, not a credential.

projectStructure.grain: the associations model sample (see associations.sample); not a sample of it

logPsfVariance.method: one-way decomposition: between-project share = sum over projects of n_g (mean_g - mean)^2 divided by the total sum of squared deviations of log(psf); descriptive, no model

projectStructure.meaning: the access indicators are nearly project-level constants (transactions of one project share one location), and price variation is dominated by differences BETWEEN projects; an unadjusted with-vs-without facility comparison on this population would compare project means, so this pack labels its model a between-project comparison and conditions on no project identity

perProjectMedianPsf.unit: SGD per square foot (median of the shipped psf column, per project)

responseLineage.check: psf equals price/area_sqft for every condo row: 245655/245655 exact (max deviation 0.0)
responseLineage.definition: price (nominal SGD) per square foot of strata area

scope: RS05 facility-premiums evidence: measured absence of the legacy in-house facility layer, join-key (project_name) recovery and coverage, per-facility no-record status, a between/within-project variance decomposition, and one recorded descriptive OLS of log condo price-psf on five jointly-fitted external-access indicators with stated controls (a between-project comparison; no dated prior protocol, so specification search cannot be ruled out)
